parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A dish containing 7.2 × 10⁻⁵ m³ of a substance rests on a laboratory bench. The substance is initially a liquid of density 710 kg m⁻³. Atmospheric pressure is 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa.

The liquid is heated at its boiling point so that it completely vaporises. The increase in the internal energy of the substance during this process is 17.6 kJ. The final volume of the vapour is 0.017 m³.
parts.text: Show that the magnitude of the work done on the substance when it vaporises is 1.7 kJ.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Use the information in (b)(i) to calculate the thermal energy *Q*, in kJ, supplied to the substance to cause it to vaporise.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (b)(ii) to determine a value for the specific latent heat of vaporisation *L*ᵥ, in kJ kg⁻¹, of the substance.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The substance in (b) has a specific latent heat of fusion *L*ᶠ.

Suggest and explain whether *L*ᶠ is likely to be less than, the same as, or greater than the answer in (b)(ii).
